name: v9.0.0
body:
## obsidian-mind 9.0: the vault rides inside Claude Code

Until now, everything the vault gave Claude came through hooks. Hooks have limits nobody sees.

Claude Code cuts hook output at 10,000 characters. After compaction, the session context shrank to a pointer. Subagents never got it at all. And the Stop report either reached only you, or reached Claude printed as "Stop hook error".

9.0 ships a Claude Code mod. Same vault, same scripts, a better way in.

### What changes

**Session context arrives as an instruction file**, the way `CLAUDE.md` does. It survives `/compact` and `/clear` whole. It reaches general-purpose subagents. It is no longer cut at 10,000 characters: it gets its own budget, `eager_layer_instruction_budget_bytes`, default 20,000 bytes. `/memory` lists it as `.claude/session-context.md`.

**The Stop report becomes one line under the answer.** `obsidian-mind: vault check: 1 note(s) marked done but still in active/`. That's all you see. Claude gets the full report with your next message, unseen. Once per change, never repeated, and it survives `claude --resume`.

**Hooks work after `/cd`.** Every hook command now finds the vault root from a subfolder.

### Proven, not assumed

A new delivery gate asks the model itself what context it received: at startup, after `/compact`, after `/clear`, and from a subagent. It passes every checkpoint on Claude Code 2.1.287 and 2.1.288. Its self-test runs two deliberately broken mods and fails every time, so a pass means something.

Before this release, 9.0 was back-ported by hand into two heavily customized vaults and run there until audits came back empty. 1,715 hook tests and 72 mod tests pass.

### Nothing breaks if you don't use it

Codex, Gemini, Claude Code before 2.1.287, a folder you haven't trusted: the hooks run exactly as before. The mod only loads after you accept Claude Code's trust prompt for the vault.

It is code that runs with your permissions. Read what it does first:

```bash
claude plugin validate .claude/skills/obsidian-mind
```

It lists every event the mod hooks and every call it makes. To turn it off, add `"enabledPlugins": { "obsidian-mind@skills-dir": false }` to `.claude/settings.local.json`.

### Also in 9.0

- The qmd search client no longer crashes when qmd's process dies mid-write.
- Running the test suite no longer touches your real QMD index.

---

## Quick Start

**Requirements:** [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md), [Node 22+ LTS](https://nodejs.org), and one of: [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) · [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) · [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)

**Install via [ShardMind](https://github.com/breferrari/shardmind) (recommended — wizard, optional modules, managed upgrades):**

```bash
npm install -g shardmind
mkdir my-vault && cd my-vault
shardmind install github:breferrari/obsidian-mind
```

**Or clone directly:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/breferrari/obsidian-mind.git
cd obsidian-mind
npm install -g @tobilu/qmd && qmd index && qmd embed   # optional: semantic search
```

Open the folder as an Obsidian vault, then run `claude`, `codex`, or `gemini` in the directory and type `/om-standup` (or `om-standup` in Codex).

Or download the vault zip below and extract it into your Obsidian vaults folder.

**Already using obsidian-mind?** Just tell your agent: `Update this vault to the latest obsidian-mind from https://github.com/breferrari/obsidian-mind`

## v9.0.0 — 2026-10-03

### Added
- show the Stop report as one line under the answer through the mod
- deliver session context as an instruction file through a Claude Code mod
- add om_mod flags to session-start and stop-checklist

### Fixed
- find the vault root in hook commands after /cd
- keep hook tests off the real QMD sentinel
- fail waiting qmd calls when the client's stdin breaks, instead of crashing
